description: Health and Physical Education Years 5-6 width tiers — all 19 standards
subject: Health and Physical Education

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest context in which a student can honestly be said to have met the descriptor's command term. For capability descriptors, minimum means one task context with identifiable use of the required skill. For descriptors requiring analysis, minimum requires an actual analytical move — not identification or description alone.
width_notes.typical_width: The full scope of the descriptor as ACARA elaborations define it. A student at typical has engaged with the range of contexts, situations and examples the descriptor is intended to cover — not necessarily every elaboration, but the spirit and scope of the descriptor.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions that add new task contexts, community settings, cultural perspectives or investigative angles. Wider items must genuinely extend the range of contexts, not add difficulty to the same context. First Nations elaborations are always represented where present.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations are used as source data for typical_width and as pointers to the range of intended contexts. They are not a checklist — some are examples of the same phenomenon at different specificity and have been merged. Wider may extend beyond elaborations where clearly within descriptor territory and year band.

AC9HP6M01.minimum_width: Adapt at least one locomotor or stability skill in a changed movement situation (e.g. dodging or feinting in a game, transitioning from dribbling to shooting), demonstrating a recognisable adjustment in technique in response to the changed demand.
AC9HP6M01.typical_width: Adapt and modify locomotor, stability and object control skills across a range of movement situations: dodge and feint in different game contexts; transition between skills (e.g. dribble to shoot, leap to balance) in changing situations; adapt kicking, striking and throwing skills to new games and activities; compose and perform sequences involving static and dynamic balances with rotations and direction changes.
wider: Combine surface propulsion and underwater skills in an aquatic environment — adapting familiar movement patterns to a new physical medium with different resistance and balance demands

Compose and perform a gymnastics or dance sequence requiring continuous adaptation of movement in response to timing, music or partner cues — making adaptation a responsive, ongoing process rather than a discrete step
Devise and play a modified game that forces adaptation of a known skill to a new equipment, space or rule context — designing the constraint that demands the adaptation
elaborations: applying stability and locomotor skills to dodge and feint in different movement situations
performing activities that involve a transition from one skill to another, such as from dribbling to shooting or from leaping to balancing, in changing movement situations
adapting kicking, striking and throwing skills to a variety of new games and activities
combining surface propulsion and underwater skills in an aquatic environment
composing and performing a range of static and dynamic balances on different body parts, rotating and pivoting to change direction of movement

AC9HP6M02.minimum_width: Apply a familiar movement strategy (defensive or offensive) from one game context to a different but related game context, and describe what was modified to make it fit the new situation.
AC9HP6M02.typical_width: Transfer and evaluate movement strategies across game categories: adapt defensive or offensive strategies from one invasion game to another; examine and demonstrate how strategies from one activity transfer to a new movement situation; evaluate the effectiveness of the transfer against agreed criteria; transfer balance strategies to safely traverse a natural environment.
wider: Transfer a strategy from a team invasion game to a different category of game (e.g. net/wall, target) — a category shift that requires deeper abstraction of the underlying principle
Investigate how strategies from physical games transfer to non-physical movement contexts such as dance or gymnastics sequences, and evaluate whether the transfer held
Devise a movement challenge that is deliberately designed to reward strategy transfer — and explain the structural features that make transfer possible
elaborations: adapting and transferring defensive or offensive strategies that have been successful in one game to another similar game
examining and demonstrating how strategies used in one physical activity can be transferred to a new movement situation
transferring strategies they have used to maintain balance to safely traverse a natural environment
making judgements, based on agreed criteria, about the effectiveness of transferring strategies from one game to another

AC9HP6M03.minimum_width: Experiment with adjusting one movement concept (e.g. force, speed, direction) in a specific movement activity and describe the effect on the movement outcome.
AC9HP6M03.typical_width: Investigate how multiple movement concepts (effort, space, time, objects, people) interact to improve movement outcomes: adjust force and speed to improve accuracy and control; create movement sequences with variations in flow and levels involving individuals moving in time; explore pushing and pulling movements to generate and perform counterbalances; develop spatial strategies to create tactical advantages in games.
wider: Systematically investigate two-concept combinations across different movement categories (e.g. effort+time in a throwing context; space+people in a game context; flow+levels in a sequence) and compare which combinations produce the greatest improvement in each context
Design a movement challenge specifically aimed at requiring students to manipulate a nominated concept, then test and modify it — applying the concept as a design constraint

Investigate how movement concepts from physical performance are described and used in First Nations Australian dance or movement traditions and how those concepts compare with the movement concept framework
elaborations: demonstrating an understanding of how to adjust the force and speed of an object to improve accuracy and control
creating a movement sequence that demonstrates variations in flow and levels, and involves individuals moving together in time
working with a partner to explore pushing and pulling movements and how these can be manipulated to generate and perform counterbalances
developing strategies that exploit the playing space to create overlaps and extra attackers

AC9HP6M04.minimum_width: Participate in activities of at least two different intensities, measure or observe at least one body response (e.g. breathing rate, heart rate), and use that evidence to categorise activities as low, moderate or high intensity.
AC9HP6M04.typical_width: Participate in and investigate intensity variations across a range of activity types: measure multiple body responses at different intensities; design and model warm-up and cool-down routines for the class with a rationale based on body response; connect activity intensity to health and fitness goals; categorise activities into low, moderate and high intensity using observed evidence.
wider: Investigate how heart rate responds to different types of activity (aerobic vs anaerobic, continuous vs interval) and compare patterns — introducing the concept that intensity is not just about effort level
Design an activity circuit that progressively builds intensity and includes warm-up and cool-down, then test and evaluate its effectiveness for a named health or fitness goal

Research and compare intensity recommendations from multiple sources (e.g. Australian 24-Hour Movement Guidelines, sport-specific training guidelines) and evaluate how they apply to their own activity profile
elaborations: performing activities of different intensities and measuring breathing rate, heart rate and other body responses to categorise activities into low, moderate and high intensity
designing and modelling different warm-up and cool-down routines for the class and discussing their importance for reducing the chance of injuries or soreness after activity
participating in and designing physical activity opportunities that support their health and fitness goals

AC9HP6M05.minimum_width: Participate in a physical activity in a natural or outdoor setting and describe at least one way the outdoor context enhances health or wellbeing beyond what an indoor activity would provide.
AC9HP6M05.typical_width: Participate in outdoor physical activities and analyse access and promotion: analyse how access to natural environments influences participation and wellbeing; research the Australian 24-Hour Movement Guidelines and compare to own activity habits; discuss how community place connections influence physical activity choices; analyse the steps and resources needed to promote participation in outdoor activities; consider the role of natural environments for different community groups.
wider: Learn traditional dances or movement activities from local First Nations Australian community members, examining the role these activities play in community life, cultural identity and wellbeing

Research and compare physical activity participation rates in different community settings (urban, rural, coastal) and analyse how access to natural environments shapes the types of activity available
Plan and evaluate a practical outdoor activity event for peers, including the steps, resources and access considerations needed to promote broad participation
elaborations: analysing how access to natural environments and the outdoors can influence participation in physical activities, and enhance health and wellbeing
learning traditional dances from local First Nations Australian community members and recognising the role dance plays in the lives of these communities

researching the Australian 24-Hour Movement Guidelines for Children and Young People, comparing their daily habits of physical activity to the recommendations and proposing strategies for enhancing or maintaining their levels of activity

discussing how a connection to a community space or special place can influence the types of physical activity options people will choose to participate in, such as links to skate parks, surf beaches or bushwalking trails

AC9HP6M06.minimum_width: Propose at least two strategies for their own life — one to increase physical activity and one to reduce sedentary behaviour — and explain why each is realistic given their actual circumstances.
AC9HP6M06.typical_width: Propose and explain personalised strategies for physical activity and sedentary behaviour: create and participate in an activity circuit replicable at home; research local physical activity options and their social and mental wellbeing benefits; examine benefits of physical activity for mental and social health; investigate setting up a school-based activity initiative; connect strategies explicitly to both increasing activity and reducing sedentary time as distinct goals.
wider: Research the physical activity and sedentary behaviour patterns of a specific community group (e.g. older adults, working parents, people in different geographic settings) and propose strategies tailored to that group's constraints — applying the strategy-design logic to a context beyond themselves

Design and pilot a school-based intervention (lunchtime competition, activity circuit, playground games) aimed at increasing physical activity levels for students and staff, and evaluate its effectiveness
Compare physical activity and sedentary behaviour recommendations across different health guidelines and explain any differences in terms of target population or health goal
elaborations: creating and participating in an activity circuit they could replicate at home that is designed to improve health-related fitness
examining the benefits of physical activity for social health and mental wellbeing, and researching options for participating in physical activities in the local area

investigating the resources needed and steps required to set up a lunchtime sports competition, activity circuit or playground games aimed at increasing levels of physical activity among students and staff

AC9HP6M07.minimum_width: Make a prediction about which movement solution will be most effective for a specific movement challenge, test at least one solution, and evaluate the result against the prediction using a specific criterion.
AC9HP6M07.typical_width: Predict, test and refine movement solutions across a range of situations: predict and systematically test solutions to unfamiliar movement challenges; co-develop criteria to assess effectiveness; adapt movement skills from other contexts to generate solutions to outdoor movement challenges; test and refine multiple solutions against criteria; explain which solution was most effective and why.
wider: Apply the predict-test-refine cycle to a complex tactical problem in an invasion game — predicting the effect of a strategic change, testing it in a modified game, and evaluating effectiveness against agreed performance criteria
Investigate how elite athletes or coaches use prediction and systematic testing in their preparation, and compare this professional process to the students' own predict-test-refine cycle
Design a movement challenge specifically intended to have no obvious solution, requiring systematic testing across multiple approaches, then evaluate the challenge design as well as the solutions
elaborations: predicting and systematically testing a range of solutions to unfamiliar movement challenges to find out which solution is most appropriate or effective
adapting movement skills and strategies from other contexts to generate creative solutions to unfamiliar movement challenges when participating in outdoor activities

co-developing criteria to assess effectiveness of responses to movement challenges, predicting the effectiveness of each, then testing and refining solutions against the criteria in order to achieve successful outcomes

AC9HP6M08.minimum_width: Identify one structural feature of a game that creates unfairness or exclusion, propose a specific rule or condition modification that addresses it, and test whether the modification improved the situation.
AC9HP6M08.typical_width: Devise, test and evaluate game modifications for fair play and inclusion: propose changes to rules or conditions to create a more inclusive game or fairer contest; recognise unfairness and exclusion in game situations and propose structural remedies; test modifications in practice and evaluate their effectiveness; discuss where and when fairness and inclusion have been observed and what structural conditions enabled them.
wider: Investigate the rules and structural features of traditional First Nations Australian games (such as Inkanyi and Barambah gimbe) specifically to understand how the game structure itself promotes participation and inclusion — comparing these structural features with those of conventional competitive games
Design an original game from scratch with inclusion and fair play as explicit design constraints, test it with peers, and document the design decisions that were made to achieve the equity goals

Research how major sporting codes have modified rules over time to improve inclusivity or fairness (e.g. modified formats, adaptive sport rules) and evaluate whether the modifications achieved their goals
elaborations: proposing changes to rules and/or conditions to create a more inclusive game or to allow for a fairer contest
recognising unfairness and exclusion in a game situation, and proposing strategies to overcome these issues
discussing where and when they have witnessed fairness and inclusion in a game situation and explaining what factors led to the game being inclusive and fair

investigating the effectiveness of rules used in traditional games of First Nations Australians to promote participation, such as Inkanyi: a cooperative running game played by the Pitjantjatjara / Yankunytjatjara of central Australia where there are no winners and Barambah gimbe: a throwing and catching game from the lands of the Wakka Wakka where catchers can be nominated to increase participation

AC9HP6M09.minimum_width: Participate in a group movement activity demonstrating at least one encouraging behaviour and negotiating at least one role or responsibility using a named communication strategy.
AC9HP6M09.typical_width: Participate positively across the full range of group participation demands: explore and perform different roles and responsibilities; demonstrate negotiation skills during conflicts or disagreements; use reflective listening and assertive communication in group movement tasks; encourage others through specific, context-appropriate behaviours; sustain positive participation across the arc of a group activity.
wider: Lead a small group through a complex movement challenge requiring multiple rounds of role negotiation and conflict resolution — applying all participation skills in a sustained leadership context

Reflect on and compare group participation across different activity types (team sport, cooperative outdoor challenge, creative movement task) and identify which participation skills are most important in each context

Investigate how collaborative participation norms differ across cultural contexts — including traditional movement activities — and discuss how these differences influence what 'positive participation' looks like
elaborations: exploring and performing the different roles and responsibilities in physical activities that promote enjoyment, safety and positive outcomes for participants
demonstrating negotiation skills when dealing with conflicts or disagreements in movement situations
using reflective listening and assertive communication when working in small groups on movement tasks or challenges

AC9HP6P01.minimum_width: Identify at least two types of people or relationships that influence identity and explain how each contributes to the way a person sees themselves, with at least one concrete example.
AC9HP6P01.typical_width: Explain how identity is shaped by both people and places: how role models, peers, family, popular culture, gender stereotypes and media influence developing identities; how connection to people and places influences personal and cultural identity over time; how beliefs and cultural practices contribute to positive self-identities; how these understandings inform strategies for creating positive self-identities.
wider: Investigate how First Nations Australians identify within and across communities through connection to Country/Place — including cultural group, clan, skin names and social standing — examining how this identity framework differs from and extends beyond Western individual identity models
Examine how beliefs and cultural practices of Australians of Asian heritage convey meanings and contribute to positive self-identities — comparing with students' own cultural identity sources
Explore how connection to people and places changes during major life transitions and what this means for identity maintenance and construction
elaborations: explaining how role models influence the way individuals see themselves; for example, sporting role models, social media influencers, parents, friends and coaches

investigating how First Nations Australians identify within and across communities through connection to Country/Place; for example, Bama People of the rainforests of North Queensland or Quandamooka People of South East Queensland
examining how beliefs and cultural practices convey meanings for cultural groups, including Australians of Asian heritage, and contribute to the development of positive self-identities
exploring how connection to people and places can influence personal and cultural identities over time
exploring the different levels of connection within First Nations Australian communities, such as cultural group, clan, Country/Place, skin names and social standing within community
exploring how family, peers, popular culture, gender stereotypes and the media influence developing identities

AC9HP6P02.minimum_width: Describe at least three physical changes associated with puberty, acknowledge that experiences differ, and identify at least one type of resource or strategy available for managing the changes.
AC9HP6P02.typical_width: Investigate the range of resources and strategies for managing puberty and transitions: understand that experiences of puberty differ and management choices are personal; examine physical products and resources for managing physical changes including menstruation; discuss how families and cultural groups acknowledge developmental stages; analyse how roles and responsibilities change as people grow older; understand the developmental link between puberty and reproduction.
wider: Investigate the connection between puberty and rites of passage ceremonies in First Nations Australian communities, examining how cultural practices support young people through developmental transitions and comparing these with other cultural acknowledgements of development
Research how different cultural groups and families celebrate and acknowledge major stages of development, examining what these practices communicate about community values and expectations
Examine how media representations of puberty and adolescence shape expectations, and compare media representations with reliable health information — identifying where media diverges from reality
elaborations: understanding that experiences of puberty differ, and the resources and strategies chosen to manage these changes are personal
examining the range of products and resources available to manage the physical changes associated with puberty, including products for managing menstruation
understanding that physical changes experienced during puberty are linked to rites of passage ceremonies in many First Nations Australian communities
discussing ways families and cultural groups acknowledge and celebrate major stages of development in young people's lives
analysing how roles and responsibilities change as people grow older and examining strategies for managing these increasing responsibilities
examining how the developmental changes that occur through puberty prepare a persons' body for reproduction

AC9HP6P03.minimum_width: Identify one example of a gender stereotype in a text or media representation and explain how it influences expectations about roles or responsibilities.
AC9HP6P03.typical_width: Investigate how gender stereotypes influence portrayal of societal roles and responsibilities: identify characters in texts who do or don't conform to traditional gender stereotypes; examine how social and cultural norms about gender influence family and community roles; identify limiting and harmful effects of gender stereotypes; question the fairness of gender roles; propose strategies to advance gender equality and respect for human rights.
wider: Investigate how gender norms vary across different cultural contexts and time periods, examining what these variations reveal about the social construction of gender roles rather than their inevitability
Analyse how sport and physical activity contexts reinforce or challenge gender stereotypes — examining media coverage, participation patterns and the narratives told about male and female athletes

Research examples of individuals who have challenged gender stereotypes at significant personal cost and examine the conditions that made it possible for them to do so, connecting to human rights frameworks
elaborations: identifying characters in texts who are not constrained by traditional gender stereotypes and how this influences their choices and actions
questioning the fairness of gender roles and proposing ways to challenge those practices that infringe on an individual's human rights
investigating how social and cultural norms about gender can influence the roles and responsibilities of family members and people within their community
identifying those gender norms that can have limiting and harmful effects, and proposing strategies to advance gender equality and respect for human rights

AC9HP6P04.minimum_width: Demonstrate at least one expression of respect and one of empathy in a role-play scenario and describe the effect on the relationship.
AC9HP6P04.typical_width: Describe and demonstrate respect and empathy across a range of relationship contexts: explore strategies for responding when relationships change; propose strategies for managing bullying and harassment and building new friendships; demonstrate respect and empathy in physical activity group roles; recognise how language directed at First Nations Australians can cause offence; examine behaviours that constitute bullying, racism or gender-based violence versus respectful behaviours.
wider: Investigate the specific language that can cause offence to First Nations Australians and develop language awareness strategies — examining how word choices affect relationship quality and trust in cross-cultural contexts

Analyse case studies of public figures who have demonstrated respect and empathy in challenging situations (e.g. across cultural difference, following conflict or controversy) and identify the specific behaviours that constituted the respect and empathy
Practise expressing respect and empathy in online communication contexts, examining how the absence of non-verbal cues changes what is required to communicate these qualities effectively
elaborations: exploring strategies for responding when relationships change, such as starting a new school, changing priorities or interests, family break-up, or joining a new sports team
proposing strategies for managing the changing nature of relationships, including dealing with bullying and harassment, and building new friendships
exploring and performing different roles and responsibilities in physical activities that promote enjoyment, safety and positive outcomes for all participants
recognising how words and labels used regarding First Nations Australians can cause offence and how this awareness can support and strengthen respectful relationships
examining the behaviours people demonstrate when treating others in respectful ways, and comparing to those behaviours that constitute forms of bullying, racism or gender-based violence

AC9HP6P05.minimum_width: Describe at least one strategy for promoting diversity or addressing discrimination in a specific community context, and explain the steps involved in implementing it.
AC9HP6P05.typical_width: Describe and implement diversity strategies across community contexts: propose strategies to help others understand different viewpoints; discuss how adaptations enable inclusivity in physical activities; explore initiatives that sporting and cultural groups use to counter discrimination and support wellbeing; examine the bystander role in challenging discrimination; discuss the role of cultural expression in maintaining connection to Country for First Nations Australians.
wider: Explore the importance of First Nations Australian cultural expressions in maintaining connection to Country/Place and examine how these cultural practices contribute to community wellbeing, identity and belonging — and how this differs from non-Indigenous cultural expression

Research how sporting organisations (local, national or international) have implemented diversity and inclusion initiatives and evaluate their effectiveness, identifying which structural features made them more or less successful

Examine how beliefs, values and cultural practices of Australians of Asian heritage influence people's sense of identity and belonging, and propose strategies to strengthen cultural inclusion in their own school or community context
elaborations: proposing strategies to help others understand points of view that differ from their own and to encourage discussion about individual and cultural similarities and differences to tackle discrimination such as sexism, racism and homophobia
exploring initiatives that sporting and cultural groups use to celebrate diversity, counter discrimination and racism, and support the wellbeing of their communities
discussing the role bystanders can play in promoting respectful interactions and challenging disrespect and discrimination such as homophobia, transphobia and racism
discussing how adaptations and modifications to physical activities can enable inclusivity for students with a range of abilities
exploring the importance of cultural expressions of First Nations Australians in maintaining a continuing deep connection to Country/Place and its influence on wellbeing
examining how beliefs, values and cultural practices convey meaning and influence peoples' sense of identity and belonging, including Australians of Asian heritage

AC9HP6P06.minimum_width: Identify an emotional response in an interaction context and apply at least one strategy to manage that emotion, describing the effect on the interaction.
AC9HP6P06.typical_width: Apply strategies and analyse emotional influence across contexts: explore emotions associated with feeling unsafe or uncomfortable and strategies to manage them; analyse how emotions influence decision-making in peer-group, family and movement situations; explore intense and unpredictable emotional responses including grief; practise self-regulation strategies for strong emotions; connect emotion management to interaction quality.
wider: Analyse a series of case studies involving emotionally charged decision-making (peer pressure, family conflict, grief) and compare which self-regulation strategies were most effective in each type of situation — building a contextualised strategy repertoire

Investigate how emotional responses in physical activity and sport contexts can be intense and public, and develop strategies specifically for managing emotional expression in these high-stakes, visible situations
Examine how different cultural norms around emotional expression influence interactions, and discuss how awareness of these differences can help navigate cross-cultural interactions
elaborations: exploring the emotions associated with feeling unsafe or uncomfortable and proposing strategies to manage these situations
analysing situations in which emotions can influence decision-making, including in peer-group, family and movement situations

exploring when emotional responses can be intense or unpredictable, including feelings of grief associated with loss, and practising strategies to self-regulate and manage expression of strong emotions

AC9HP6P07.minimum_width: Describe the four steps of consent communication and rehearse seeking or giving consent in at least one scenario using both verbal and non-verbal communication.
AC9HP6P07.typical_width: Describe and rehearse consent strategies across contexts: practise the four steps (asking, responding, listening, reacting) explicitly; rehearse verbal and non-verbal consent communication; practise interpreting non-verbal cues related to giving and denying consent; explore and rehearse managing emotional responses when consent is denied (disappointment, shame, anger); analyse how denial of consent can affect others' feelings and practise constructive responses.
wider: Apply consent communication skills across a range of real-world contexts including physical contact, personal space, online image sharing and social media interactions — examining how the same consent principles operate differently across contexts with different power dynamics
Investigate how consent communication norms have changed historically and culturally, and discuss what this reveals about the relationship between consent and respect for individual autonomy

Design and evaluate a consent education resource for peers, applying understanding of the four steps and common communication challenges — requiring students to translate their knowledge into a teaching artefact
elaborations: exploring the steps of seeking, giving or denying consent (asking, responding, listening and reacting) and practising how to communicate their intentions effectively at each step
practising and refining strategies for interpreting verbal and non-verbal cues related to seeking, giving and denying consent in a range of situations

analysing how a person's reaction to being denied permission to do something can affect others' feelings and discussing options for dealing with situations when this may occur; for example, feelings of disappointment, shame and anger associated with rejection

AC9HP6P08.minimum_width: Analyse at least one scenario in which a protective behaviour or help-seeking strategy was used, explain what made it effective or ineffective, and describe at least one online safety strategy and how to report harmful online behaviour.
AC9HP6P08.typical_width: Analyse and rehearse protective behaviours and help-seeking across online and offline contexts: research reliable help sources; examine ways to normalise and de-stigmatise help-seeking; discuss strategies for online safety including reporting; explore actions when feeling unsafe online; propose bystander strategies for supporting others in unsafe situations; analyse media characters' responses to unsafe situations and evaluate their efficacy.
wider: Investigate the specific online environments students use (social media, gaming, messaging) and develop tailored safety strategies for each — going beyond generic online safety advice to context-specific protocols
Design and deliver a peer education activity on online safety or help-seeking, requiring students to translate their analysis of effective strategies into a teaching format
Examine research on help-seeking stigma in young people and propose evidence-based strategies for their own school community, connecting to existing school support structures
elaborations: researching sources of health information and places where they can seek help, and prioritising those that are reliable and trustworthy
examining ways to normalise and de-stigmatise help-seeking behaviour so all students feel more comfortable and confident to seek help when needed
discussing strategies for maintaining online safety when using digital tools and environments, including the options and processes for reporting negative or harmful behaviour

exploring actions they can take when they feel unsafe when online; for example, who to speak to if someone posts an embarrassing picture of them without permission or when to step away from negative online social interactions
proposing strategies they can use if they witness others in unsafe situations, such as accessing support networks or telling an adult they trust
analysing the responses of characters in TV shows or movies when in unsafe or risky situations and discussing the efficacy of their response to the situation

AC9HP6P09.minimum_width: Compare health information from at least two different source types on the same topic, identify which is more reliable and explain why using at least one specific reliability criterion.
AC9HP6P09.typical_width: Investigate health information sources and apply findings to choices: examine how family, friends, media and public identities influence health choices; analyse nutritional information and develop strategies to communicate healthier choices; identify trusted people for health concerns and rehearse communication; compare health information from different sources and verify accuracy and reliability; connect reliable information to personal and others' health decisions.
wider: Investigate how misinformation about health topics spreads through social media and community networks, develop specific fact-checking strategies, and evaluate the reliability of commonly shared health claims
Research Australian public health campaigns and evaluate how they balance accuracy, accessibility and motivation — applying reliability and communication quality criteria

Compare health information about the same topic across sources aimed at different audiences (children, adults, health professionals) and examine how source purpose and audience shape the information presented
elaborations: examining how family, friends, media and public identities may influence the way people act and the choices they make in relation to their health
analysing nutritional information of different foods and developing strategies to communicate healthier choices to their family
identifying trusted people in their lives with whom they can share their health needs and concerns, and rehearsing ways to communicate concerns about their health to a variety of support people
examining and comparing relevant health information and opinions, and identifying which aspects can be verified as accurate and reliable

AC9HP6P10.minimum_width: Analyse one behaviour and explain its effect on health or wellbeing at both an individual and community level, identifying at least one community-scale mechanism.
AC9HP6P10.typical_width: Analyse how behaviours influence community health across domains: recognise safety actions including contamination prevention, infection control and anaphylaxis awareness; investigate healthy living practices including diet, physical activity and social connection; explore kinship structures in First Nations Australian communities and their role in community wellbeing; propose strategies to increase physical activity and reduce sedentary behaviour at community level; practise assertive communication in situations involving inappropriate behaviour; evaluate positive online community contribution.
wider: Investigate how kinship and extended family structures in First Nations Australian communities support and enhance health, safety and wellbeing — examining how these community structures create a different model of health support than individualised or nuclear family models
Research sustainable food practices and examine the quality of food available in a local context (school canteen, local area), proposing strategies to improve both sustainability and nutrition

Examine how social connection and belonging contribute to mental health and wellbeing at community scale — including research on loneliness, belonging and community cohesion — and propose strategies to strengthen social connection in their school community
elaborations: recognising actions that can help keep classmates safe, including strategies to reduce potential for contamination, infection and anaphylaxis

investigating practices that help promote and maintain health and wellbeing, such as eating a diet reflecting The Australian Guide to Healthy Eating, meeting recommendations for daily physical activity and creating connections with others to enhance social health
exploring how kinship and extended family structures in First Nations Australian communities support and enhance the health, safety and wellbeing of their communities
proposing strategies they can use in daily routines to increase physical activity levels and reduce sedentary behaviour
practising and refining assertive communication techniques that can be used in a range of situations where they may be asked to do something they don't believe is appropriate
proposing and implementing strategies to positively contribute to online environments, such as evaluating the impact of 'character' behaviour when gaming with peers
examining sustainable food practices to measure the quality of food available in the school canteen or local area
describing strategies to support a sense of belonging and connection, and recognising the importance of social support for enhancing mental health and wellbeing
